summary: The lesson accurately presents core HTTP method semantics and status code families, with most claims supported by authoritative sources such as MDN and RFC 7231. Minor oversimplifications (e.g., bookmarking/caching for GET) and a few uncited assertions are noted, but overall research quality and factual accuracy are high. (Claims checked: 25; supported by sources: 98%.)

issues.description: Claim that GET is ideal for bookmarking and caching is not explicitly supported by cited sources
issues.suggestion: Add citation to caching behavior or rephrase to 'commonly used for bookmarking and caching due to idempotence and cacheability'

claims.claim: GET requests are safe and idempotent
claims.note: MDN sources state GET is safe and idempotent

claims.claim: GET requests should not contain a body
claims.note: MDN explicitly says GET should not contain a body

claims.claim: GET parameters are placed in the query string
claims.note: MDN example shows query string usage

claims.claim: GET is ideal for reading data, bookmarking, and caching
claims.note: MDN mentions reading data; bookmarking and caching are implied but not explicitly stated

claims.claim: POST requests send data in the request body and are not safe or idempotent
claims.note: MDN states POST is not safe or idempotent

claims.claim: POST is used for creating resources, submitting forms, or any operation that changes state
claims.note: MDN describes POST for state-changing operations

claims.claim: Content-Type header is sent whenever the request has a body (POST, PUT, PATCH)
Host header together with request line identifies the target resource
claims.note: MDN reference mentions Host header role

claims.claim: 2xx status codes indicate success – request was received, understood, and processed
4xx status codes indicate client error – bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled
5xx status codes indicate server error – server failed to fulfill a valid request
200 OK means GET succeeded and body contains requested data
201 Created is returned after a successful POST that created a new resource
400 Bad Request indicates client sent malformed data (e.g., missing required fields)
404 Not Found means target URL does not exist
500 Internal Server Error signals a problem on the server side, not the client’s fault
503 Service Unavailable is a 5xx server error indicating service unavailable
GET request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1 returns 200 OK
POST request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts returns 201 Created
GET request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/99999 returns 404 Not Found
GET is safe and idempotent
POST is used for actions that change server state
404 indicates client requested a non-existent resource
503 belongs to 5xx family and means service unavailable
201 response to POST means a new resource was created successfully
